member.name: T:DotNetCore.HealthChecks.HayateOpHealthCheck`1
member.summary: A Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks probe over a single object pool.

remarks.para: Three questions are asked, in this order, and the first one that fails decides the result:

item.description: Is the pool's own circuit breaker open? Then nothing can be borrowed at all — Unhealthy.
Are all concurrent slots busy? The pool still works, but the next borrower waits — Degraded.
If an is configured, does a real borrowed object still work? A bad answer is Unhealthy.

remarks.para: The third question is the only one that can cost anything, so it is asked last and only when it can be answered without waiting: a health check that blocks is worse than one that reports less, so when every slot is busy the probe is skipped and the degraded answer stands.

member.name: T:DotNetCore.HealthChecks.IHayateObjectHealthProbe`1
member.summary: Decides whether a single pooled object is still usable — the protocol-level question the pool itself cannot answer.

remarks.para: A pool knows how many objects it holds and whether its own circuit breaker is open, but it has no way to tell whether a pooled connection still answers. That answer needs a round trip, and only the code that owns the protocol can make it. This interface is the seam: the pool supplies the mechanism — borrow an object, hand it over, take the verdict, give the object back — and the implementation supplies the meaning, which for a connection pool is a PING and for anything else is whatever "still works" means there.

The probe is optional: without one, reports exactly what it reported before it existed. It is also only consulted when an object can be borrowed without waiting — a health check that blocks is worse than a health check that says less, so when every slot is busy the probe is skipped and the pool is reported as degraded rather than probed.

One borrowed object per check is the whole cost. Implementations should therefore be cheap and bounded: the check runs on whatever schedule the host configured, and a probe that hangs hangs the check.

member.name: M:DotNetCore.HealthChecks.IHayateObjectHealthProbe`1.IsHealthyAsync(`0,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.param: An object borrowed from the pool for the duration of this call.
Cancels the probe when the health check itself is cancelled.
member.returns: true when the object is usable; false to fail the health check.
member.remarks: The object is returned to the pool as soon as this method completes, on every path — including the throwing one. Implementations must not release it themselves, and must not keep a reference to it afterwards: once this method returns, the next borrower owns it.
